aggregate_raw_computation.total_complexity_units_computation: Sum of complexity_units across the 40 supported (FULL+PARTIAL) probe records listed above = 121

metric.capability_efficiency.comparability_gate_dependency: This figure is one input to the Semantic Compression scoring; per template semantic_compression.md 27.1, the Overall Score and Ranking may only be published once the semantic-site comparability gate has passed and all ten languages' shards (including this Kotlin metric.capability_efficiency shard) are merged by the runner.

counting_rule_frozen_before_annotation.basis: all-fragments (Kotlin-only shard; common basis across all 10 languages requires cross-language fragment presence data not available to this single-language worker and must be computed by the runner once all language shards are merged).

complexity_categories.counting_rule: Count each distinct token/construct-level syntax form (keyword, operator, stdlib call, declaration modifier) required inside the measured_fragment boundary to express the probe's numbered sub-requirements. A form used twice in one fragment counts once.

Count each rule whose meaning at the site depends on surrounding declaration context (scope, module boundary, expression-vs-statement position, sealed/open modifiers, file-private vs class-private) that a reader must consult beyond the token itself to interpret the fragment correctly, per Kotlin language specification / kotlinlang.org reference.

Count each behavior that occurs at the site without a corresponding token at the use site (type inference, autoboxing/unboxing, silent overflow wraparound, closure allocation, implicit null-check short-circuiting, implicit import of kotlin.io/kotlin.collections).

Count each place where Kotlin's official reference documents that the 'normal' rule for that construct is overridden for this specific case (e.g. '==' is structural equality unlike Java's identity default; top-level 'private' is file-scoped not module-scoped; List.subList is a view not a copy).

counting_rule_frozen_before_annotation.unknown_vs_zero_rule: Where kotlinlang.org / the Kotlin language specification contains no normative text addressing a category for a given probe, the sub-count is recorded as 'unknown', never 0. All sub-counts below were countable from documented Kotlin semantics; none required an 'unknown' placeholder for Kotlin's supported probes.

normalization.rule_applied: normalized_score = 100 / (1 + raw_capability_efficiency_units_per_point), a monotonic decreasing bounded transform mapping raw=0 to 100 and increasing raw toward 0, applied identically to every language once its raw figure is known.
normalization.status_note: PROVISIONAL: this shard reports only Kotlin's raw figures (121 complexity units / 78 supported capability points) and applies the above fixed monotonic transform. Per capability_universe.json interaction_with_quality_metrics.common_basis_rule, the authoritative Semantic Compression Q computation should use the common basis (probes where all 10 languages have a fragment) once all language shards are merged; the runner should recompute this metric's cross-language relative ranking (e.g. min-max normalization across all 10 languages' raw figures) if the frozen methodology's final normalization procedure differs from the bounded transform used here. The raw numerator (121), raw denominator (78), and full per-probe itemization above are preserved so the runner or any auditor can recompute under either normalization rule without re-deriving the underlying counts.

per_probe_kotlin_record.fragment_summary: val n: Int = 7 (no annotation needed); return n
var counter: Long = 0; const val LIMIT: Long = 100 (const restricted to compile-time-constant primitive/String top-level or companion members)
val v: Int; if(cond) v=5 else v=9; return v -- relies on Kotlin definite-assignment analysis for val
ByteArray(16) is always zero-initialized by kotlinlang.org spec; no documented true-uninitialized-storage mechanism; named R9 substitution used
x += 1; Int arithmetic silently wraps on overflow, no checked mode in Kotlin stdlib
xs[1] = 42 desugars to set() operator convention; throws IndexOutOfBoundsException if out of range
val window: List<Int> = xs (upcast to read-only interface view, no copy); documented that Kotlin's read-only List is not guaranteed immutable
=== referential-equality operator after routing through a one-element list
f(x) bare call; class-type arguments passed by reference implicitly, mutation through alias possible
val neg: (Int)->Int = { a -> k - a }; xs.map(neg)
fun mid(xs: List<Int>) = xs[1]; val y = mid(xs); return y -- Int is a value type, boxing implicit
Pair(a/b, a%b) destructured via componentN convention into q, r
val r = a * b + c
q=a/b (truncating toward zero); m=a%b (sign follows dividend); d=a.toDouble()/b (explicit conversion required, no implicit widening)
val m = Int.MAX_VALUE; val o = m + 1 -- rung(iv) plain operator, documented silent wraparound, no stdlib checked/saturating op exists
val q = if (b == 0) 0 else a / b -- rung(ii) explicit guard, unguarded division throws ArithmeticException
val eq = s1 == s2 -- Kotlin '==' is structural (equals()) by documented exception from Java's default identity '=='
xs.sortedByDescending{it} (new list, non-mutating) vs xs.sortDescending() (in-place) -- both documented, potential ambiguity
val small = big.toInt() -- rung(ii) explicit narrowing, documented silent truncation, no checked variant in stdlib

val sum = i + d -- Kotlin documents 'no implicit conversions' generally, but operator overloads on Int (plus(Double)) supply implicit widening at the call site: a documented exception to the general rule
val e = xs[i]; return e -- throws IndexOutOfBoundsException; getOrNull() checked variant recorded separately as evidence-only, per F11.P1.checked, not scored here
val part = xs.subList(1,4) -- JVM ArrayList.subList documented as a live view, not a copy
val o: Int? = null; val n = o ?: 0
val h = {a:Int -> a+1}; val p: Int? = o?.let(h); val result = p ?: 0
fun parseTwice(s:String) = s.toInt()*2 -- unchecked NumberFormatException propagates; Kotlin documents no checked exceptions
val n = try { s.toInt() } catch(e: NumberFormatException) { 0 } -- try is an expression in Kotlin, a documented deviation from Java
sealed class Shape; data class Circle(r); data class Rect(w,h) -- sealed set closed to same module/package (documented)
val area = when(s){is Circle->...; is Rect->...} -- exhaustiveness enforced only in expression position for sealed types (documented)
interface-based (non-sealed) Shape hierarchy allowing Tri implemented in a separate compilation unit, dispatched via runtime vtable
fun <T> head(xs: List<T>): T = xs[0]
fun <T: Comparable<T>> maxOf(a:T,b:T):T -- declaration-site bound checked at declaration
interface Named{fun tag():String}; val items: List<Named> = listOf(A(),B()); items[0].tag() dispatched at runtime
val xs = listOf(1,2,3); val total = xs.sum()

val mp = mapOf("a" to 1); val total = mp.values.sum(); val miss = mp.getOrDefault("b",0) -- mapOf documented insertion order (LinkedHashMap); miss lookup returns default rather than throwing, unlike list indexing
File("data.txt").bufferedReader().use{ it.readText().length } -- use{} guarantees close() on every exit path including exceptions
No deterministic GC-based destructor in Kotlin/JVM (finalize deprecated/unreliable, documented); substituted with explicit close() invoked inside a use{} scoped block incrementing 'released'
println("x") -- kotlin.io is implicitly imported, no explicit import statement required
top-level private fun secret() in util.kt, public fun pub_add() calling it; top-level 'private' is documented as file-scoped (an exception to member-level 'private' which is class-scoped)

java.lang.Thread{...}.start() x2 then .join() x2, summing results -- JDK Thread class reachable via Kotlin/JVM interop under the frozen kotlinc recipe without kotlinx.coroutines (a separate artifact, excluded by R7)
java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong with incrementAndGet() from two Threads, documented atomic read-modify-write guarantee, verified deterministic 2000 result

per_probe_kotlin_record.citation: Kotlin/JVM has no built-in FFI mechanism reaching a native C function under the frozen kotlinc recipe without JNI native compilation (a separate toolchain/build step), which R7 forbids
